heroHeadline: ARTEMIS III CREW REVEAL 9 DAYS AWAY (JUNE 9, JSC) — FAA IFT-12 INVESTIGATION ONGOING; 3 MOON BASE LAUNCHES TARGETING 2026; ARTEMIS II CREW DAY 51
heroSubtitle: May 31: The Artemis III crew announcement at Johnson Space Center is 9 days away (June 9, 11 a.m. EDT, NASA+/YouTube). The four astronaut names for the redesigned LEO rendezvous-and-docking test mission (targeting late 2027) will be revealed publicly for the first time; NASA credentialed international media for the event before the May 28 RSVP deadline. Artemis III will fly with a structural spacer replacing the ICPS (the sole remaining ICPS is reserved for Artemis IV/first crewed lunar landing 2028); MSFC is fabricating the barrel and ring components. The FAA's mishap investigation into Starship IFT-12 (Booster 19 boostback burn failure, May 22) remains open: SpaceX is working on a corrective-action report under FAA oversight, and IFT-13 (Ship 40 + Booster 20, V3) cannot receive a flight license until the report is approved — analysts project return-to-flight no earlier than July–August 2026. This delays the orbital propellant transfer demonstration (a mandatory Artemis III HLS qualification milestone requiring two Starships docking in LEO) to Q3-Q4 2026 at the earliest. On the Moon Base front, three uncrewed robotic missions are now targeting calendar year 2026: Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mark 1 Endurance lander to Shackleton Connecting Ridge (Moon Base I, fall 2026), Astrobotic's Griffin lander with Astrolab's FLIP rover (Moon Base II), and Intuitive Machines' Nova-C Trinity with the Lunar Vertex payload (Moon Base III). The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen — are on Day 51 post-splashdown at JSC. The Artemis II Orion is in de-servicing at KSC's Multi-Payload Processing Facility; the heat shield ships to Marshall Space Flight Center this summer for X-ray scans and Avcoat sample extractions that will define Artemis IV crewed landing readiness. House Appropriations full-committee markup (May 13) recommends $24.438B for NASA flat with FY2026 — rejecting the White House's 23% cut.
